userStories.title: Migrate rate limiter from in-memory Map to a persistent store for Vercel deployments
userStories.description: The current rate limiter (src/lib/chat/rate-limit.ts) uses a module-level in-memory Map. On Vercel, each serverless function invocation may run in a separate isolate, making the store non-persistent and allowing rate limit bypass through request distribution across instances. This is a security gap for the public orders and chat endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria: Rate limit state is stored in Neon Postgres or Vercel KV instead of an in-memory Map
A single IP submitting 6 orders within one hour from any Vercel instance is correctly blocked on the 6th request
The rate limiter table/store is automatically cleaned up (TTL or cron-based) to prevent unbounded growth
Localhost/127.0.0.1 exemption is preserved for automated tests
429 response includes Retry-After header as currently implemented
Rate limiter logic is covered by at least 3 unit tests: allow, block, and reset-after-window
technicalNotes: Simplest Neon-based approach: CREATE TABLE rate_limit_log (ip TEXT, endpoint TEXT, window_start TIMESTAMPTZ, count INT, PRIMARY KEY (ip, endpoint, window_start))
Use ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET count = count + 1 for atomic increment
Alternative: Vercel KV (Redis) with INCR + EXPIRE for atomic sliding window — lower latency than Postgres for hot paths
The chat endpoint already uses a more complex dual-window model; preserve that behavior
For /api/orders: window = 1 hour, max = 5; these limits should be configurable in env vars

On Vercel (and most serverless platforms), the filesystem is read-only — writes silently fail or throw, breaking the payment upload flow in production. Files must be stored in Vercel Blob, AWS S3, or equivalent.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/orders/[id]/payment uploads the screenshot to Vercel Blob (or configured S3 bucket) instead of the local filesystem
The returned screenshotUrl is a publicly accessible HTTPS URL, not a /uploads/... relative path
The order record in Neon stores the full external URL in payment_screenshot_url
Admin panel can display the screenshot by rendering the external URL in an tag
Upload fails gracefully (400 error) if the configured storage credentials are missing in env
OWASP file validation (MIME type allowlist, magic bytes check, 5MB size limit) is preserved after migration
No files are written to the local filesystem in the new implementation
technicalNotes: Use @vercel/blob with put() for simplest Vercel-native integration; requires BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN env var
Alternatively use AWS S3 PutObject with @aws-sdk/client-s3 and pre-signed URLs
Preserve the UUID-based filename sanitization (safeId logic) — prepend orderId to blob name
Existing magic byte validation (MAGIC_BYTES record in route.ts) is already correct — keep it
Add NEXT_PUBLIC_STORAGE_PROVIDER env var ('vercel-blob' | 's3' | 'local') to allow local-dev fallback

userStories.description: The project has no HTTP security headers configured. Without X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, browsers may sniff uploaded image files as HTML — creating an XSS vector through the payment screenshot upload. X-Frame-Options prevents clickjacking on the payment page. A Content-Security-Policy reduces script injection risk.

The app still functions correctly in EN/MS/ZH locales with the CSP active (no console CSP violations)
technicalNotes: Add async headers() to next.config.ts returning the header array for source: '/(.*)'
CSP must allowlist: 'unsafe-inline' for Tailwind CSS style injection (or use nonces), next/image optimization domain, Groq/OpenRouter API domains for connect-src, Google Fonts for font-src
The PWA docs explicitly show this security header pattern — reference nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/progressive-web-apps
Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) is better applied at the Vercel/CDN level than in Next.js headers()

userStories.title: Enable static rendering on [locale] pages by implementing setRequestLocale
userStories.description: next-intl requires setRequestLocale() to be called in every layout and page that participates in static rendering. Without it, all locale-prefixed pages opt into dynamic (SSR) rendering, negating Next.js ISR and static build optimizations. For a menu page with revalidate = 3600, the failure to call setRequestLocale means every request hits the server instead of a cached response.
acceptanceCriteria: setRequestLocale(locale) is called at the top of the [locale]/layout.tsx render function
setRequestLocale(locale) is called in all [locale]/* page components that receive locale from params

technicalNotes: Import setRequestLocale from 'next-intl/server' and call it before any await in the component body
generateStaticParams must return [{ locale: 'en' }, { locale: 'ms' }, { locale: 'zh' }]

userStories.title: Add WhatsApp notification delivery retry with exponential backoff for order submissions
userStories.description: Order submission currently sends a WhatsApp notification to the waiter as a fire-and-forget call. If the WhatsApp API call fails (network timeout, rate limit, provider outage), the order is saved but the waiter receives no notification — the cafe misses the order entirely. A retry mechanism with exponential backoff should be implemented.
acceptanceCriteria: Failed WhatsApp API calls are retried up to 3 times with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s delays)
After all retries are exhausted, a structured error is logged with the order ID for manual follow-up
The order is always saved to Neon first, before any notification attempt — a notification failure never rolls back the order save

The notification retry logic is unit-tested: successful on retry, exhausted retries, and partial failure scenarios
technicalNotes: Implement a simple async retry helper: async function withRetry(fn, retries=3, baseDelayMs=1000)
The WhatsApp send call currently lives in the orders route — extract it to src/lib/notifications.ts for testability
Add notification_status TEXT DEFAULT 'pending' column to the orders table in the migration script
For a more robust solution, consider a background job (Vercel Cron) that re-attempts failed notifications every 5 minutes, querying WHERE notification_status = 'failed'
WhatsApp Business API best practice: respond 200 to webhook immediately, then process async

userStories.title: Use Neon pooled connection string and prevent connection leaks in serverless route handlers
userStories.description: The db.ts Neon client uses the standard connection URL. On Vercel (serverless), each function invocation may open a new TCP connection that isn't properly closed, eventually exhausting PgBouncer's max_connections. The Neon docs specifically recommend using the pooled connection string (-pooler suffix) for serverless environments.
acceptanceCriteria: DATABASE_URL in production uses the Neon pooled connection string (hostname ending in -pooler.neon.tech)
A separate DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED env var is available for migrations (which require session mode)
.env.example is updated to document both variables and when to use each
No SET search_path statements or session-level configuration in any route handler (incompatible with PgBouncer transaction mode)
All schema-qualified queries use explicit schema.table notation instead of relying on search_path
A load test of 50 concurrent order submissions completes without 'too many clients' errors
technicalNotes: In src/lib/db.ts, the neon() call should use DATABASE_URL which points to the pooled endpoint
The @neondatabase/serverless driver over HTTP is optimal for single-query routes (all current routes qualify)
The inline DDL (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS) in route handlers is a connection-count concern — coordinate with the migration script story
PgBouncer transaction mode limitation: temporary tables, SET statements, and SQL-level PREPARE are unavailable — audit all queries for these patterns

userStories.title: Extract inline DDL from API route handlers into a proper migration script
userStories.description: The orders route handler contains CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and multiple ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS statements that run on every request. This creates unnecessary DB round-trips on each order submission, slows response time, and is incompatible with Neon pooled connections in transaction mode. Schema changes belong in a migration script run once at deploy time.
acceptanceCriteria: All CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS statements are removed from API route handlers
A new scripts/migrate.ts (or .sql) file contains all table creation and column addition DDL
package.json includes an npm run db:migrate script that executes scripts/migrate.ts against DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED
Vercel deployment runs npm run db:migrate automatically before npm run build (via vercel.json buildCommand or package.json build script prefix)
Route handler response time for POST /api/orders improves by at least 50ms (no DDL round-trip)
CI pipeline runs npm run db:migrate in a test step to validate the migration is idempotent
technicalNotes: Use the direct (unpooled) connection string for migrations since they may require session-level commands
Structure migration as numbered files (001_create_orders.sql, 002_add_payment_columns.sql) for auditability
The site_settings table creation in site-settings.ts (ensureTable()) has the same problem and should be migrated too
Alternatively use a lightweight migration library (postgres-migrations, db-migrate) or write a single idempotent migrate.ts
dependencies: Use Neon pooled connection string and prevent connection leaks in serverless route handlers

userStories.title: Add skip-to-content link and landmark roles to the public layout
userStories.description: The site has no skip navigation link, meaning keyboard and screen reader users must tab through the entire header before reaching the main content. WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks) requires a mechanism to skip repetitive navigation. Landmark roles also help screen reader users jump directly to sections.
acceptanceCriteria: A 'Skip to main content' link is the first focusable element in the DOM, visible on focus, and targets <main id='main-content'>
The <header>, <main>, <footer>, and nav elements use correct semantic HTML landmark roles
The chat widget and tray widget floating buttons have appropriate aria-label descriptions
Screen reader test confirms the page can be navigated by landmarks (region navigation in NVDA/VoiceOver)
The skip link is visually hidden until focused, then appears above the header (position: fixed, z-index above header)
technicalNotes: Add Skip to content as the first child of in [locale]/layout.tsx
Add id='main-content' to the <main> element in the layout
Verify the Header component uses <header> semantic element and the Footer uses <footer>
The floating chat widget and tray widget should use aria-label to describe their purpose

userStories.title: Implement dynamic og:image generation per locale using Next.js ImageResponse
userStories.description: The current OG image is a single static /images/og-image.jpg for all pages and locales. Social shares of individual blog posts show a generic cafe image instead of the actual content. Next.js App Router supports dynamic OG image generation via ImageResponse that can render the post title and cafe name in the correct locale.
acceptanceCriteria: Blog post pages generate a dynamic og:image showing the post title and cafe name in the post's locale
The OG image renders correctly at 1200x630px with readable text
The generated image is cached by Next.js (revalidate matches the page's ISR revalidate period)
Fallback to the static /images/og-image.jpg when the dynamic image generation fails
Facebook and Twitter card debugger tools show the correct per-page og:image URL
Menu page OG image shows the cafe name and 'Menu' label in the active locale
technicalNotes: Create src/app/[locale]/blog/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx exporting ImageResponse
Use the Next.js edge-compatible ImageResponse from 'next/og'

Keep the static og-image.jpg as the root layout fallback — only generate dynamic images for blog and menu pages

userStories.title: Add global-error.tsx and per-route error boundaries
userStories.description: The app has no error.tsx files in any route segment and no global-error.tsx at the app root. Unhandled exceptions in RSC rendering currently crash the entire page with no fallback UI or recovery option. Next.js App Router requires client-side error boundaries (error.tsx) at each segment level and a global-error.tsx that owns html/body for root-layout crashes.
acceptanceCriteria: app/global-error.tsx exists with its own <html><body> wrapper, a user-friendly message in all 3 locales, and a reset() button
app/[locale]/error.tsx exists and catches segment-level rendering errors with a bilingual fallback and reset button
Errors thrown by RSC data fetches (e.g. DB timeout) render the error boundary instead of a blank page
Error digest is logged to console (not exposed to users)
Error boundary does not catch errors inside event handlers (those are handled with useState)
technicalNotes: error.tsx must be a Client Component ('use client')
global-error.tsx must include <html> and <body> tags — it replaces the root layout
Use useEffect(() => console.error(error), [error]) in the error component for server-side log correlation
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling

userStories.title: Add PDPA-compliant privacy notice and data collection disclosure
userStories.description: Malaysia's Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (Act 709) requires any commercial website collecting personal data (name, phone number, payment screenshots) to inform users of the purpose of collection, their rights, and the data controller identity. The site currently collects phone numbers and payment screenshots with no privacy notice anywhere. Non-compliance exposes the operator to compound penalties.
acceptanceCriteria: A privacy notice page exists at /[locale]/privacy and is linked in the footer of all locales
The order submission modal displays a brief inline disclosure: 'Your contact number is used only to notify you about this order. See Privacy Policy.'
The payment upload page displays a disclosure that the screenshot is used solely for payment verification and deleted after confirmation
Privacy notice covers: data controller identity (cafe name + contact), data collected, purpose, retention period, user rights (access, correction, deletion)
Privacy notice is available in EN, MS, and ZH
Footer link renders as a Next.js <Link> to avoid full page reload
technicalNotes: Malaysia PDPA 2010 (Act 709) Section 7 — Notice and Choice Principle: data subjects must be informed before or at time of collection
Data controller registration with Jabatan Perlindungan Data Peribadi (JPDP) may be required for commercial operators
Reference: https://www.pdp.gov.my
Store privacy page content in messages/{locale}.json for i18n consistency

userStories.title: Add visible focus indicators for all interactive elements
userStories.description: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7 (Level AA) requires a visible focus indicator for all keyboard-operable UI. A global CSS reset or Tailwind's default outline removal frequently strips focus rings from buttons, links, and form inputs. The order form, tray widget, filter pills, and admin panel buttons all need verified, high-contrast focus indicators.
acceptanceCriteria: All interactive elements (buttons, links, inputs, selects, checkboxes, filter pills) have a visible focus ring when navigated via keyboard
Focus indicators use :focus-visible (not :focus) to avoid showing rings on mouse clicks
Focus ring meets WCAG 2.4.7: minimum 2px outline, 3:1 contrast against adjacent colours
Tailwind's focus:outline-none is not applied to any interactive element without a custom replacement
Verified by keyboard-only navigation through: home page → menu filter → add to tray → order form → submit
technicalNotes: Add to globals.css: :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--primary); outline-offset: 2px; } as a global fallback
Audit all shadcn/ui component overrides for focus:outline-none and replace with focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-primary
WCAG 2.4.7 Level AA applies; 2.4.11 Enhanced Focus Appearance is WCAG 2.2 Level AA
Reference: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/focus-visible.html

userStories.title: Add accessible inline form validation error messages to order form
userStories.description: WCAG 2.1 SC 3.3.1 and 3.3.3 (Level AA) require that when input errors are detected, a text description is provided and correction suggestions are given. The current order form validates phone number and ETA client-side, but error feedback relies on HTML5 browser validation bubbles which are not reliably screen-reader accessible.
acceptanceCriteria: Phone number field shows an inline error message with aria-live='polite' when the format is invalid, explaining the expected format (e.g. '01X-XXXXXXXX')
ETA picker shows an inline error when time is less than 15 minutes from now, with a suggestion: 'Earliest arrival is [calculated time]'
Each error message is linked to its input via aria-describedby
Error messages appear below the input field and persist until the user corrects the value
Error state is visually indicated with a red border + error icon (not colour alone — WCAG 1.4.1)
Form cannot be submitted while validation errors are present
technicalNotes: Replace HTML5 browser validation bubbles with React-controlled error state
Use aria-invalid='true' on fields in error state

Pattern:

{error}
WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 3.3.3 Error Suggestion — both Level AA
Reference: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/error-suggestion.html

userStories.title: Add CSP nonce for inline scripts to strengthen Content Security Policy
userStories.description: The layout injects JSON-LD via dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and Tailwind v4 may inject inline styles. Without a nonce, a strict CSP cannot block 'unsafe-inline' for scripts without breaking these legitimate inline elements. A per-request nonce generated in middleware enables strict CSP without disabling XSS protection. This is complementary to the security headers story (already complete) which sets a permissive baseline CSP.
acceptanceCriteria: A cryptographically random nonce is generated per request in middleware.ts
The nonce is passed to the layout via a request header (x-nonce)
All inline <script> tags in the layout (including JSON-LD components) receive the nonce attribute
The Content-Security-Policy header uses nonce-{value} instead of 'unsafe-inline' for scripts
No browser console CSP violations on any page in production mode
The nonce changes on every page load (not static)
technicalNotes: Use crypto.randomUUID() to generate the nonce: const nonce = Buffer.from(crypto.randomUUID()).toString('base64')
Pass nonce via response header: response.headers.set('x-nonce', nonce)
Read nonce in layout via headers(): const nonce = (await headers()).get('x-nonce')
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/content-security-policy
Tailwind v4 uses CSS custom properties (not inline styles) — verify before adding style-src nonce

userStories.title: Add MenuSection schema.org structured data for individual menu items
userStories.description: The existing RestaurantJsonLd and MenuPageJsonLd provide top-level Restaurant and Menu schema, but Google's rich results can also index individual menu items (MenuItem, MenuSection) enabling price and item name display directly in search results. This is a significant SEO opportunity for a food ordering site.
acceptanceCriteria: The /[locale]/menu page renders a schema.org Menu with nested MenuSection (one per category) and MenuItem entries
Each MenuItem includes: name (locale-matched), description, offers.price, offers.priceCurrency (MYR), offers.availability (based on item availability status)
Unavailable items use offers.availability: OutOfStock
Structured data validates without errors in Google Rich Results Test
Schema is rendered server-side as a <script type='application/ld+json'> tag
MenuSection groups items by their POS category
technicalNotes: Use @type: MenuItem within @type: MenuSection within @type: Menu
Reference: https://schema.org/MenuItem and https://schema.org/MenuSection
Fetch menu data server-side in RSC and pass to a JsonLd component — do NOT expose all items to the client bundle
Limit to available items only or mark unavailable with correct availability property to avoid misleading rich results

userStories.title: Add Web Vitals reporting with useReportWebVitals hook
userStories.description: There is currently no Core Web Vitals measurement or reporting. Without field data, it is impossible to know whether LCP, INP, and CLS targets are being met on real Malaysian mobile connections. The Next.js useReportWebVitals hook provides built-in access to all CWV metrics and can send data to any analytics endpoint.
acceptanceCriteria: A WebVitals client component uses useReportWebVitals to capture LCP, INP, CLS, FCP, and TTFB
Metrics are logged or sent to an analytics endpoint (e.g. /api/vitals or Vercel Speed Insights) on each page load
The component is added to the root layout and does not block rendering
LCP threshold alert: log a warning when LCP > 2500ms in development mode
The implementation adds zero JavaScript weight to the initial page render
technicalNotes: useReportWebVitals is a Next.js Client Component hook — add to a dedicated 'use client' component
Free option: @vercel/analytics and @vercel/speed-insights packages provide zero-config CWV monitoring on Vercel deployments
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-report-web-vitals
Vercel Speed Insights: npm i @vercel/speed-insights then <SpeedInsights /> in root layout

userStories.title: Add database indexes on orders table for admin dashboard queries
userStories.description: The orders table has no indexes beyond the primary key. The admin Orders panel queries by status and created_at for filtering and sorting. As order volume grows, full table scans will increase serverless function execution time and Neon compute cost. Missing indexes are the highest-impact query optimization for serverless Postgres.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration script adds: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_orders_status ON orders(status)
Migration script adds: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_orders_created_at ON orders(created_at DESC)
A composite index is added: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_orders_status_created ON orders(status, created_at DESC)
EXPLAIN ANALYZE output for the admin orders query shows Index Scan instead of Seq Scan after migration
Indexes are added to the existing migrate.mjs script as idempotent steps using IF NOT EXISTS
technicalNotes: Neon Serverless driver executes each query as a separate HTTP round-trip; slow queries multiply latency
A partial index on active statuses only (WHERE status NOT IN ('ready', 'rejected')) would reduce index size for the most common admin view
Reference: https://neon.com/docs/guides/nextjs
Test with EXPLAIN ANALYZE before and after adding indexes on Neon's SQL editor

userStories.title: Add Suspense streaming boundaries to slow data-fetching page sections
userStories.description: Next.js App Router's streaming capability allows fast page shells to render immediately while slow data fetches complete in the background. The menu page, home page highlights section, and blog listing all make Neon DB queries server-side. On Vercel, cold-start plus Neon round-trip can add 500-1500ms before any content is visible. Suspense boundaries with skeleton fallbacks decouple fast and slow sections.
acceptanceCriteria: The menu page hero (static) renders immediately; the menu grid is wrapped in a <Suspense> boundary with a skeleton fallback matching the MenuGrid layout
The home page highlights section is wrapped in <Suspense> with a skeleton fallback
The blog listing page wraps the post grid in <Suspense>
Each Suspense boundary has a dedicated loading skeleton that matches the content dimensions (prevents CLS when content loads)
Streaming is verified with network throttling showing content arriving in chunks before DB data is ready
technicalNotes: Move static content (hero, nav) above the Suspense boundary; move DB-dependent content inside it
loading.tsx is already present for /[locale] and /[locale]/menu — ensure they match actual page skeleton dimensions to prevent CLS
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data#streaming
For the admin panel, use React.lazy + Suspense for tab panels that are not initially visible

userStories.title: Enhance robots.txt to block AI training crawlers and locale-prefixed admin paths
userStories.description: The existing robots.ts disallows /api/ and /admin/ but does not account for locale-prefixed admin variants or Vercel's internal /_next/data/ paths. It also lacks rules to block AI training crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot) which is increasingly expected for content-focused sites.
acceptanceCriteria: robots.ts disallows /api/, /admin/, /kds/, and /_next/data/
A separate rule set blocks AI training crawlers (GPTBot, anthropic-ai, CCBot, ChatGPT-User) from all paths
The sitemap URL in robots.txt uses the NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL env var (dynamic, not hardcoded)
robots.ts uses MetadataRoute.Robots type for type safety
Visiting /robots.txt returns correct directives with no 404
technicalNotes: robots.ts already exists and is partially correct — this is an enhancement, not a new file
AI crawlers to block: GPTBot, anthropic-ai, CCBot, ChatGPT-User, Google-Extended (optional per operator preference)
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/robots
Note: robots.txt is advisory only — it does not prevent determined crawlers

userStories.title: Optimize Interaction to Next Paint (INP) for tray and menu filter interactions
userStories.description: INP is a Core Web Vital with a 200ms threshold. The tray widget and category filter pills involve React state updates that re-render large component trees (entire menu grid re-renders on filter change). Long tasks on the main thread from JavaScript execution block these interactions from meeting the INP threshold on low-end Android devices.
acceptanceCriteria: Filter pill selection shows immediate visual feedback within 50ms of tap (before menu grid re-renders)
Adding an item to the tray shows immediate count badge increment before any complex state updates
Menu grid filtering is deferred using React's startTransition to mark it as non-urgent
INP measured with Lighthouse mobile simulation is < 200ms on the /menu page
No individual JavaScript task on the main thread runs > 50ms during filter interactions
technicalNotes: Wrap menu grid re-renders in startTransition: const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition(); startTransition(() => setFilter(cat))
Show filter pill as 'active' immediately (optimistic update), then let the grid catch up
Consider virtualization (react-window or @tanstack/virtual) if the menu has > 50 items
Reference: https://web.dev/articles/inp
Test on a throttled mobile CPU profile in Chrome DevTools Performance tab

userStories.title: Prevent Cumulative Layout Shift from menu card images loading
userStories.description: CLS threshold is 0.1. Menu cards show food images that load asynchronously. Without explicit aspect ratio containers, images cause layout shift as they load, which can cause accidental taps on wrong items — a critical UX failure for a food ordering app. The shift also directly degrades Google PageSpeed score.
acceptanceCriteria: All menu card image containers have an explicit aspect ratio set via CSS (aspect-ratio: 4/3 or equivalent) before the image loads
Next.js Image components in menu cards use explicit width and height or fill with a sized container
CLS score on /[locale]/menu measured by Lighthouse is < 0.1
No layout shift occurs when menu images load on a throttled 3G connection
Blog post card images also have explicit containers to prevent CLS on the blog listing page
technicalNotes: Use CSS: .menu-card-image-container { aspect-ratio: 4/3; position: relative; overflow: hidden; }
For Next.js Image with fill: wrap in a div with explicit height or aspect-ratio
Reference: https://web.dev/articles/cls
Avoid using top/left for animation; use transform: translate() instead

userStories.title: Add revalidateTag-based cache invalidation for menu and blog updates
userStories.description: Admin menu and blog edits currently call revalidatePath with hardcoded locale paths (e.g. '/en/menu', '/ms/menu', '/zh/menu') — three separate calls that are fragile, miss related pages, and don't work with the Next.js Data Cache layer. Using revalidateTag provides a single locale-agnostic invalidation that works across the full cache hierarchy.
acceptanceCriteria: Menu data fetch functions in src/lib/menu.ts tag their fetches with next: { tags: ['menu'] } via unstable_cache
Admin PATCH/POST routes for menu items call revalidateTag('menu') instead of multiple revalidatePath calls
Adding a new locale requires no code changes to the cache invalidation logic
Home page highlights are also invalidated when menu data changes
Blog post routes use revalidateTag('blog') and admin blog mutations call revalidateTag('blog')
technicalNotes: Since src/lib/db.ts uses the Neon HTTP driver (not fetch), wrap DB calls with unstable_cache and pass tags: ['menu']
revalidateTag works across all locales simultaneously — no need to enumerate locale paths
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/caching#fetch-optionsnexttags-and-revalidatetag
Note: revalidateTag inside a Route Handler does NOT invalidate the client Router Cache — only Server Actions do that immediately

userStories.title: Configure Vercel function region to Singapore for minimal Malaysia latency
userStories.description: Vercel deploys serverless functions to a default region (typically iad1 — US East) unless explicitly configured. For a Malaysian cafe serving customers in Johor/KL, this adds 200-400ms of unnecessary latency to every server-side request. Configuring the function region to Singapore (sin1) significantly reduces TTFB for the target audience.
acceptanceCriteria: vercel.json is created or updated with a regions configuration specifying sin1 (Singapore)
The Neon database branch is confirmed to be in aws-ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) to minimize DB round-trip latency
TTFB measured from Malaysia is < 400ms after the change
The region setting does not conflict with Edge runtime usage (Edge runs globally regardless)
vercel.json is committed to the repository
technicalNotes: Add to vercel.json: { "regions": ["sin1"] } — Singapore is the closest Vercel region to Malaysia
Neon database should be in aws-ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) to co-locate with the function
Reference: https://vercel.com/docs/functions/configuring-functions/region
Vercel Hobby plan supports 1 region; Pro supports up to 3 regions for failover

userStories.title: Add bundle analyzer and lazy-load heavy admin panel dependencies
userStories.description: The admin panel may import heavy client-side libraries that are bundled into the main JavaScript chunk. Next.js production checklist recommends @next/bundle-analyzer to identify large modules and dynamic import() for components not needed on initial render. Admin panel JavaScript weight should not affect the customer-facing page load.
acceptanceCriteria: @next/bundle-analyzer is installed as a dev dependency and configured in next.config.ts
Running ANALYZE=true npm run build produces an HTML bundle report
Any admin panel component or dependency > 50KB (gzipped) is converted to a dynamic import with a loading skeleton
The main customer-facing JavaScript bundle does not include any admin-only component code
Admin panel tab components (Orders, Settings, Blog editor) are lazy-loaded on first tab activation
technicalNotes: Install: npm i -D @next/bundle-analyzer
Configure in next.config.ts: withBundleAnalyzer({ enabled: process.env.ANALYZE === 'true' })(nextConfig)
Use Next.js dynamic(): const AdminBlogEditor = dynamic(() => import('./admin-blog-editor'), { loading: () => <Skeleton /> })
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/package-bundling#analyzing-javascript-bundles
Target: customer page JS bundle < 150KB gzipped; admin bundle can be larger since it is auth-gated

userStories.title: Add order expiry mechanism for stale pending_approval orders
userStories.description: Orders in pending_approval status that are never acted on accumulate indefinitely. There is no expiry or timeout logic. For a manual-review workflow, stale orders clutter the admin panel, inflate unread count badges, and leave customers in a perpetual pending state. A background cleanup or on-read expiry resolves this.
acceptanceCriteria: Orders in pending_approval older than 4 hours are automatically transitioned to an 'expired' status
The expiry check runs on each GET /api/admin/orders request before returning results (lazy expiry), or via a Vercel Cron Job
Expired orders are filterable in the admin Orders tab
The customer-facing /order/[id] page shows an 'Order expired — please re-order' message for expired orders
The expiry threshold (4 hours) is configurable in site settings or env var
technicalNotes: Simplest implementation: run UPDATE orders SET status='expired' WHERE status='pending_approval' AND created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '4 hours' at the start of the admin orders fetch
Alternatively use a Vercel Cron Job calling /api/admin/cron/expire-orders (Hobby plan: 1 cron job, daily minimum interval)
Add 'expired' to the order status enum/type definitions
Add an index on (status, created_at) — covered by the database indexes story
dependencies: Add database indexes on orders table for admin dashboard queries

userStories.title: Add offline fallback page for PWA users
userStories.description: The service worker implements network-first navigation with cache fallback, but there is no dedicated offline fallback page. When a customer has no connectivity and navigates to a URL not in the shell cache, they get the browser's generic offline page instead of a branded experience. PWA best practices require a custom offline page.
acceptanceCriteria: A static offline.html page exists at public/offline.html with the cafe branding and a 'You are offline' message in all 3 languages
The service worker caches /offline.html during the install event
When a navigation request fails and no cached match exists, the SW responds with the offline page
The offline page includes the cafe name, logo reference, and a 'Try again' button
The offline page renders correctly with no external resource dependencies (all CSS inline or from cache)
technicalNotes: Add '/offline.html' to SHELL_URLS in public/sw.js
In the fetch handler: caches.match(event.request).then(cached => cached || caches.match('/offline.html'))
Keep offline.html fully self-contained (inline styles) to avoid sub-resource fetch failures
Reference: https://web.dev/articles/pwa-checklist
Update CACHE_NAME version string when modifying sw.js to trigger cache refresh

userStories.title: Add aggregateRating to Restaurant JSON-LD from admin-configurable value
userStories.description: Google's LocalBusiness rich results can display star ratings in search results when aggregateRating is present in the Restaurant JSON-LD schema. The existing RestaurantJsonLd component does not include aggregateRating. Adding a configurable rating to SiteSettings and surfacing it in the schema enables potential star rating display in Google Search.
acceptanceCriteria: site-settings schema gains optional fields: ratingValue (number 1-5), ratingCount (integer), and ratingProvider (string)
Admin Settings tab exposes these fields as optional inputs with validation
RestaurantJsonLd includes aggregateRating only when ratingValue is set — never includes placeholder values
If ratingValue is not configured, aggregateRating is omitted entirely
Validated with Google Rich Results Test showing no warnings for the aggregateRating block
technicalNotes: Never fabricate rating data — only use actual ratings from a verifiable source (e.g. real Google Maps reviews)
Google requires reviewCount >= 1 to display stars; a single verified Google review qualifies
Schema property: aggregateRating: { '@type': 'AggregateRating', ratingValue: '4.8', reviewCount: '47' }
Reference: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/local-business
